title: The Number of the Smallest Unoccupied Chair
statement: `n` friends, numbered `0` to `n - 1`, come to a party that has an unlimited row of chairs numbered `0, 1, 2, ...`. `times[i] = [arrival_i, leaving_i]` gives the moment friend `i` arrives and the moment they leave. On arrival, a friend sits in the lowest-numbered chair that is empty at that moment. A chair becomes empty at the exact moment its occupant leaves, so a friend arriving at that same moment may take it. No two friends arrive at the same moment. Return the number of the chair taken by friend `targetFriend`.
notes:
## Intuition

Replaying the party in arrival order and scanning chairs `0, 1, 2, ...` for an empty one works, but each arrival can scan many chairs, so it is O(n²). Two questions repeat at every arrival: "which seated friends have left by now?" and "which empty chair has the smallest number?". A min-heap answers each quickly: one heap of seated friends ordered by leaving time, and one heap of returned chairs ordered by number. Chairs never used before are handed out by a counter, because any brand-new chair is larger than every chair already in use.

## Approach

1. Sort friend indices by arrival time into `order`.
2. Keep `occupied` (entries `[leaving, chair]`), `freeChairs` (entries `[chair]`) and `nextChair = 0`.
3. For each `friend` in `order`, pop every `occupied` entry whose leaving time is at most `arrival` and push its chair into `freeChairs` (`<=` because a chair freed at this moment may be reused now).
4. The friend takes the smallest freed chair if there is one, otherwise `nextChair`, which then moves up by one.
5. If this is `targetFriend`, return the chair; otherwise push `[leaving, chair]` into `occupied`.

## Example 1, step by step

`times = [[1,4],[2,3],[4,6]]`, `targetFriend = 1`. The arrival order is friends 0, 1, 2.

- Friend 0 arrives at 1: nothing has left, no freed chairs, so chair `0` (`nextChair` becomes 1).
- Friend 1 arrives at 2: friend 0 leaves at 4 > 2, so nobody is popped; chair `1` comes from the counter. Friend 1 is the target, so the answer is `1`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n log n): the sort, plus at most one push and one pop per friend on each heap.
- Space: O(n) for the order and the two heaps.

## Pitfalls

- Release chairs whose leaving time equals the arrival time; using `<` instead of `<=` gives a chair that should be free to nobody.
- Process friends by arrival time, not by index: the input is not sorted.
- Release every departed friend before choosing, since a lower chair may have been freed later than a higher one.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `order` | friend indices sorted by arrival time |
| `occupied` | min-heap of `[leaving, chair]` for seated friends |
| `freeChairs` | min-heap of chairs that were used and are empty again |
| `nextChair` | smallest chair number never used yet |
| `friend`, `arrival`, `leaving` | the friend being seated and their times |
| `chair` | the chair that friend takes |
| `push`, `pop` | heap helpers comparing entries by their first value |
